subject: different outcomes old dartR version vs DartR 2.0.4

messages.author: 722521532a54784f
messages.subject: different outcomes old dartR version vs DartR 2.0.4
parts:
Hi everyone,
I had done an analysis in DartR with the previous DartR version, and now that the new DartR (v 2.0.4) is available, I installed this new version and re-did my analysis with it (as before I was using some functions from the developer version, i.e. gl.filter.sexlinked, and some functions from the established previous DartR version..).

I used the same filtering thresholds as the previous analysis, and most results are the same but there are a few differences, such as:
- gl.report.secondaries: 
  • new DartR version (2.0.4) reports 56307 invariant sequence tags, 
  • while the previous DartR version reports only 56305 (although the number of filtered secondaries SNPs is the same betweem the 2 DartR versions)
- gl.filter.sexlinked: with t.het 0.60 and t.hom 0.05 --> 
  • new DartR version (2.0.4) filters 56 sex-linked loci, 
  • while the previous DartR version reports only 53 sex-linked loci
- gl.outflank:
  • new DartR version (2.0.4) filters 170 outliers
  • previous DartR version filters 174 outliers...

What are these differences due to as the filtering thresholds used are the same? Are there any differences in these functions in the new dartR version?
I would really appreciate some help understanding what could have caused these differences...

Thanks a lot
Best,
Gabriella

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] different outcomes old dartR version vs DartR 2.0.4
parts:
Hi Gabriella,

In regards to gl.filter.secondaries, this function strips all but one SNP from each sequence tag, where the sequence tag happens to have been scored for more than one SNP. It, by default, selects one SNP at random, so you would expect slightly different results from one run to another.

With gl.report.secondaries, your question relates to the estimate of sequence tags that are invariant. The function does this by fitting a zero truncated Poisson distribution to the distribution of 'SNP frequencies per tag', then extrapolates to estimate the value for the zero class. This again, uses approximate techniques to achieve convergence to a solution, which has a small random element to it.  So you would expect slightly different results from one run to another.

gl.filter.sexlinked has undergone some serious re-coding between the two versions, which could explain why it is slightly more efficient in the latest version. Luis might be able to assist here.

Ditto gl.outflank.

You might also check if you have exactly the same filtering prior to the application of these functions in the two versions.

Hope this helps.

A

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] different outcomes old dartR version vs DartR 2.0.4
parts:
Hi Arthur,
sorry for the late reply, I thought I had submitted my reply already...

I used the "best" method in gl.filter.secondaries, so that's why I get a different estimate of invariant sites in the gl.report.secondaries (compared to the previous dartR version) but the same number of secondaries when I filter.
As for gl.outflank and gl.filter.sexlinked then I will just assume that the newer functions are better in the newest DartR version.

I just had another question or better feedback on the new dartR version as I realized that apparently all the "report" functions, such as gl.report.reproducibility, gl.report.callrate, gl.report.maf, gl.report.rdepth report the number of loci/individuals retained by quantile instead of by specific thresholds (i.e. 0.25, 0.60, etc..) as it was done in the previous dartR version...would there be an option to get the number of individuals/loci retained for a specific threshold used (i.e. 0.60) instead of only for quantile percentages directly on the report outcome (as previously) (instead of trying filtering with different thresholds - i.e. 0.25, 0.60, 0.80) and find out only after each filtering how many individuals/loci were affected/removed?

I am sure that there is a good reason why you have changed the outcome of the report for all these functions, and probably is more valid statistically to base the decision on the threshold to filter with on quantile rather than on random percentage values, however, I found the previous report version more practical when trying to figure out if there was only some outlier individuals/loci at specific threshold values (i.e. 0.25, 0.60)...I am not sure if that makes sense...?

Thanks a lot anyways 
Best,
Gabriella
